title: The Tank That Floated Out of the Ground

beats.text: This is Max. It just went wrong.
Max had a plan. How hard could it be, really?
It failed, because Untreated sewage soaks straight down with its solids and germs into the water people pump from wells.
So Max fixed it, and it held, because Still water lets heavy solids sink and fats float, so the liquid separates into layers.
It failed, because A watertight box with no exit just fills up and the sewage comes back the way it came.
So Max fixed it, and it held, because Soil and its microbes filter and treat the liquid before it reaches groundwater.
It failed, because With nothing blocking the outlet, solids and grease escape and clog the gravel's pores.
So Max fixed it, and it held, because A pipe that dips below the surface only drinks from the clear middle layer.
It failed, because An empty tank in saturated soil is like a boat: groundwater pushes it up harder than its weight holds it down.
So Max fixed it, and it held, because Ballast weight strapped to the tank outweighs the groundwater's upward push.
Now every fix works together, and it holds. Which fix would you build?
